pure-announcement.rationale: A benchmark research paper with transferable findings about skill design, not a product launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: The existing agent-skills-format concept covers what Skills are, while this source adds efficacy measurement and the focused-beats-exhaustive finding a reader would not learn there.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Claims trace to a primary arXiv paper describing a reproducible benchmark with deterministic verifiers and paired conditions.

durability.rationale: The note's central claims are pass-rate deltas on a self-described 'current inventory' of 87 tasks that has already moved through four versions, so the headline numbers will be stale within a year even though the paired-evaluation idea persists.

actionability.rationale: It gives skill authors direct guidance — measure efficacy with paired no-Skill/Skill runs, keep skills focused at three modules or fewer, and treat skills as a substitute for model scale.

atomicity.rationale: One core idea — paired evaluation shows curated, focused Skills measurably improve agent performance — with the sub-findings as evidence for it.
